result: CONCEPT organoids self-organize into concentric zones of telencephalic, optic-stalk, optic-disc, and neuroretinal tissues along the center-periphery axis, with distinct PAX2+ cell populations forming boundaries that guide RGC axon pathfinding.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly affirm this core finding. Reviewer 1 states the organoids 'exhibit remarkable pathfinding and growth of retinal ganglion cell (RGC) axons.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'The authors have succeeded in developing a robust model of optic stalk(OS) and optic disc(OD) tissue with innervating retinal ganglion cells' with 'distinct developmental and functional borders that allow for a distinct pathway for pathfinding RGC neurites.' No concerns are raised about the spatial organization or tissue identity claims.

result: RGCs in CONCEPT organoids grow directional axons that navigate toward and along PAX2+ VSX2+ optic disc cells, following a circular path defined by these adjacent cells, and exit when gaps occur in the optic disc cell population.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm the directional axon growth findings. Reviewer 2 states the model has 'a robust pattern with distinct developmental and functional borders that allow for a distinct pathway for pathfinding RGC neurites.' Reviewer 1 notes the organoids 'exhibit remarkable pathfinding and growth of retinal ganglion cell (RGC) axons.' No critiques are raised about the axon pathfinding observations or their relationship to optic disc cells.

result: Single-cell RNA sequencing of CONCEPT organoids identified 14 clusters comprising telencephalic and ocular cell types, including distinct optic disc (PAX2+ VSX2+ cluster 2) and optic stalk (PAX2+ VSX2- cells) populations with specific molecular signatures including COL9A3, COL13A1, CYP1B1, FGF8, FGF9, and an RGC cluster (cluster 11) expressing POU4F2, ATOH7, and CNTN2.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly supports this analysis, stating 'The authors compare their single-cell data of the self-forming brain-eye centroids with the published single-cell data from human fetal retinas and brain/optic organoids. This analysis further supports the similarity of their centroids with the human fetal retinal cell clusters, including the detection of the VSX2+/PAX2+ cells.' No concerns are raised about the scRNA-seq methodology, cluster identification, or marker gene expression patterns.

result: Expression signatures of optic disc cells and RGCs in CONCEPT organoids are similar to those in human fetal retinas (HGW9), with cluster 18 from fetal retinas sharing 64/113 DEGs with CONCEPT cluster 2 and showing similar PAX2, COL9A3, CYP1B1, FGF9, and CNTN2 expression patterns.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly affirms this comparative analysis: 'The authors compare their single-cell data of the self-forming brain-eye centroids with the published single-cell data from human fetal retinas and brain/optic organoids. This analysis further supports the similarity of their centroids with the human fetal retinal cell clusters.' Reviewer 3 concludes 'The new findings further support the presented centroids' applicability for future studies on human RGC development and axon guidance mechanisms.' No concerns are raised about the fetal retina comparison.

result: CNTN2 is identified as an RGC-specific cell-surface marker co-expressed with POU4F2, enabling isolation of approximately 385,000 RGCs from 100 organoids that express multiple RGC markers (TUBB3, POU4F2, ISL1, RBPMS, SNCG) and exhibit neuronal morphology.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly values this finding, stating 'The identification of cell-surface markers for RGCs could have value for understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in RGC axon development and regeneration.' All reviewers affirm the utility of the model for RGC studies without questioning the CNTN2 marker identification or isolation methodology. Reviewer 3 notes the findings 'support the presented centroids' applicability for future studies on human RGC development.'

result: Isolated RGCs exhibit electrophysiological excitability with hyperpolarized resting membrane potentials (-20.1±6.4 mV), can fire action potentials when held at -70 mV, and express functional voltage-gated sodium and potassium channels as demonstrated by TTX and TEA sensitivity.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'The strength of evidence is compelling for future studies to investigate RGC neurite outgrowth and brain-eye connectivity in humans,' implicitly accepting the functional characterization of isolated RGCs. No reviewer raises concerns about the electrophysiology data or questions the functional properties of the isolated cells. The evidence is treated as supporting the model's utility.

result: Optic disc cells differentially express FGF8 and FGF9, and FGFR inhibition drastically reduces RGC differentiation and directional axon growth, demonstrating that FGF signaling mediated by FGFRs is required for early RGC differentiation and directional axon growth in human cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly anticipates this line of investigation, stating 'Future work targeting RGC neurite outgrowth mechanisms will be exciting,' implicitly accepting the FGF signaling findings as a foundation for such work. Reviewer 1 notes the model's value 'for understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in RGC axon development,' consistent with accepting the FGF signaling mechanism. No reviewer questions the FGFR inhibition experiments or the conclusion about FGF signaling's role.

result: CONCEPT organoids contain transparent lentoid structures expressing lens markers (CRYAA, beta crystallin) that lack DAPI staining indicating denucleation, are free of organelles, and exhibit ball-and-socket structures characteristic of lens fiber cells.
evaluation: No reviewer comments on or questions the lens formation findings. The absence of critique combined with the reviewers' overall positive assessment of the organoid model ('robust model,' 'compelling evidence') suggests implicit acceptance of this supporting observation. This is treated as a confirmatory detail rather than a central finding.

result: PAX2+ optic disc/stalk, FOXG1+ telencephalic, and VSX2+ neuroretinal cell clusters found in CONCEPT organoids did not exist in Gabriel et al.'s organoids, with only 8 and 5 PAX2+ cells detected at days 30 and 60 respectively in the published dataset.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 implicitly supports this comparative analysis by affirming 'The authors compare their single-cell data of the self-forming brain-eye centroids with the published single-cell data from human fetal retinas and brain/optic organoids,' without raising concerns about the comparison with Gabriel et al.'s data. The distinction between models is accepted as supporting the novelty of the CONCEPT approach.

result: Cysts formed by embedding hESC sheets in Matrigel are hollow spheres with columnar epithelium that mimic the anterior ectoderm and efficiently generate telencephalic and ocular tissues without extrinsic factors, representing default anterior ectodermal cell fates.
evaluation: No reviewer questions the cyst formation methodology or the interpretation of default anterior ectodermal differentiation. Reviewer 2's statement that 'The authors have succeeded in developing a robust model' implicitly accepts the foundational methodology. The absence of methodological critique combined with positive overall assessments indicates acceptance of this technical approach.

result: Background claims about mammalian telencephalon-eye development, marker gene expression patterns (Foxg1, Pax6, Pax2, Fgf8), default neuroectodermal differentiation, and prior findings about Cntn2 and FGF signaling in model organisms.
evaluation: These are established background claims supported by citations to prior literature. No reviewer questions these foundational concepts, which are standard developmental biology knowledge. They provide context for the novel findings but are not themselves evaluated as new results.
